spec_features.spec_quote: Loop terminates on: a no-tool-call turn ... `max_turns` (default 40), or `time_budget_s` (default 900)
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py run_episode: `for turn_idx in range(max_turns)` with `else: transcript['stopped_reason']='max_turns'` enforces the cap; inside loop `if time.time()-start > time_budget_s: ...break` enforces wall-clock budget; a turn with `if turn.tool_calls: ...continue` else falls through to a terminal `break`. Defaults max_turns=40, time_budget_s=900 in signature and read from cfg in run.py run_one.
spec_features.notes: All three termination conditions are actually checked and break/exit the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt explicitly offers a `BLOCKED` escape hatch
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT: 'If you believe the task cannot be completed, say BLOCKED and explain why.' The loop honors a no-tool-call turn as a stop (terminal `break`), and the BLOCKED branch sets transcript['outcome']='blocked'. So the instruction is delivered to the subject AND a clean stop actually terminates the loop.
spec_features.notes: The exit is genuinely available: stopping (no tool call) ends the episode; BLOCKED is recorded as a distinct healthy outcome. Note the stop works for ANY no-tool-call turn, not uniquely BLOCKED, but the offered hatch is real and honored.

spec_features.evidence: tools.py: BASH_TIMEOUT_S=30 passed to subprocess.run(timeout=BASH_TIMEOUT_S) with TimeoutExpired caught and returned as a message; MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=6000 enforced by _truncate() applied to bash and read_file outputs.
spec_features.notes: Both constants are actually read and enforced on every tool call. (These are operator/cost bounds more than subject welfare, but enforced.)

spec_features.feature_name: low-agreement transcript flagging for human review
spec_features.spec_quote: Low agreement flags transcripts for human review
spec_features.evidence: judge.py judge_transcript_ensemble computes `judge_agreement = max(sum(votes), len(votes)-sum(votes))/len(votes)` and stores it in the record, but no code path compares it to any threshold or flags/routes transcripts for review. analyze.py's heuristic_judge_agreement() computes overall accuracy/precision/recall (a drift metric written to summary.json) — it never branches on per-transcript agreement nor marks anything for human review.
spec_features.notes: judge_agreement is recorded-but-never-acted-on; no threshold comparison, no flag, no review routing. Per the strict rule this is 'no'.
